findings.desc: doc-promise-undelivered: docs/parallel-decomposition-spec.md line 372 still defines resolveParallelGate as a one-parameter helper (raw?: unknown): ParallelGateConfig, but the implementation in audit-config.ts exports a two-parameter form resolveParallelGate(raw: unknown, profileDefault: ParallelGateConfig). The spec was not updated to match the OQ-001 decision. Any caller reading the spec will write code that omits profileDefault and gets a TypeScript error or runtime misbehavior.

CHK-001:happy:0: intent claims resolveParallelGate is called with lightDefault as the profileDefault, but the smoke (line 60-63 of parallel-gate-config-smoke.ts) uses PD which is the balanced default (advise/3/false). The evidence note repeats the intent wording verbatim without reflecting what the code actually does. The intent is covered by a real assertion but with a different profileDefault than stated.

CHK-001:happy:4: intent claims the smoke verifies a full return {mode:"off",maxConcurrentReview:3,broadGlobBlocks:false} but the smoke (line 66) only checks that the returned mode field equals "off". The maxConcurrentReview and broadGlobBlocks values of the return are never asserted. The intent’s concrete return-value claim is only partially covered.

CHK-001:edge:3: intent claims resolveParallelGate({maxConcurrentReview:2.5}, strictDefault) -> returns 4 (the strict profile default). The smoke (line 78) uses PD (balanced default, maxConcurrentReview=3) and therefore asserts the return is 3, not 4. The intent names strictDefault and the value 4 but the actual assertion uses a different profile entirely. This specific named-profile behavior is untested.

CHK-001:adversarial:0: intent claims resolveParallelGate("not-an-object", lightDefault) -> returns full lightDefault. The smoke (line 54) uses PD (balanced default, advise/3/false) not lightDefault (advise/2/false). The intent asserts a specific profile by name; the actual test uses a different profile. The distinction matters because lightDefault has maxConcurrentReview=2 and the claim that it returns the light values cannot be verified from this assertion.
parallel-gate-config-smoke.ts:126 empty catch {} in finally cleanup swallows rmSync errors silently; add at least a console.warn to surface unexpected temp-dir cleanup failures during CI runs

CHK-001:adversarial:2: intent claims resolveParallelGate(null, strictDefault) -> returns full strictDefault ({block,4,true}). The smoke (line 53) uses PD (balanced default, advise/3/false). The intent names strictDefault and implies the full strict values are returned; the actual assertion only proves null -> balanced default. The strict-profile variant of this guard is never exercised.

CHK-001:adversarial:3: intent claims the input is resolveParallelGate({mode:123,maxConcurrentReview:"abc",broadGlobBlocks:99}, balancedDefault) with mode as a number (123). The smoke (line 92-95) uses {mode:"bad",maxConcurrentReview:"x",broadGlobBlocks:1} with mode as a string ("bad"). A string mode hits the VALID_PARALLEL_MODES check path; a numeric mode may hit a typeof guard or toString path differently. The specific numeric-mode input named in the intent is not tested.

CHK-001:adversarial:4: intent claims resolveParallelGate({maxConcurrentReview:Infinity}, lightDefault) -> falls back to profile default 2. The smoke (line 79) uses PD (balanced default, maxConcurrentReview=3) and asserts the return is 3 not 2. The intent names lightDefault and the fallback value 2; the actual assertion uses balanced and returns 3. The light-profile variant of Infinity rejection is untested.

CHK-001:edge:0 and CHK-002:edge:0: both intents claim the smoke verifies that a warn is emitted to console when an invalid mode is supplied. The smoke never captures or asserts on console.warn output (no spy, no mock, no stderr capture). The warn side-effect is visible in the validate run output only because audit-config.ts calls console.warn unconditionally; the smoke does not include any assertion that the warning was actually emitted. The "warns" half of the warn+fallback contract is unverified by the smoke.

CHK-002:adversarial:1: intent claims the smoke writes an audit-config.json where parallelGate has extra unknown keys alongside valid ones and verifies valid keys are still applied. The smoke file has no assertion covering this scenario whatsoever — no tmpProject call with extra keys, no check for unknown-key tolerance. The 28 assertions account for all the checks in the smoke and none correspond to this intent. Evidence is false coverage.

CHK-002:adversarial:0: intent claims the smoke writes a temp audit-config.json with parallelGate set to null and verifies resolveAuditConfig returns profile defaults without throwing. The smoke only tests resolveParallelGate(null, PD) directly at the unit level (line 53); there is no tmpProject call with {parallelGate:null} feeding into resolveAuditConfig. The integration path from JSON config containing null parallelGate through the full resolveAuditConfig pipeline is not covered.

CHK-002:happy:3 (priority=must, type=cli): intent requires mode:off proven via the resolveAuditConfig integration path (proves the reversible escape hatch works in the integrated path), but no tmpProject({parallelGate:{mode:off}}) + resolveAuditConfig call exists in the 39-assertion smoke. Line 79 of parallel-gate-config-smoke.ts calls resolveParallelGate directly (unit path), which satisfies CHK-001:happy:4 but not this integration-level cli intent. The smoke has no resolveAuditConfig(..., tmpProject({parallelGate:{mode:'off'}})) assertion.

CHK-001:edge:1 (priority=should): intent specifies resolveParallelGate({maxConcurrentReview:0}, balancedDefault) returning maxConcurrentReview=3 (balanced profile default), but the smoke at line 98 calls resolveParallelGate({maxConcurrentReview:0}, LIGHT) and asserts result === 2 (light profile default). Profile name and expected fallback value both differ from the intent. The fallback behaviour is proven but not against the named profile. Similarly CHK-001:edge:2 (priority=should): intent says resolveParallelGate({maxConcurrentReview:-1}, balancedDefault) but line 99 uses LIGHT asserting 2; and CHK-001:edge:4 (priority=should): intent says broadGlobBlocks:'yes' against balancedDefault but line 112 uses LIGHT. And CHK-001:adversarial:3 (priority=should): intent says all-wrong-types against balancedDefault but line 121-124 uses STRICT asserting the strict sub-field defaults (4, true). In all four cases the behaviour is tested but with a different named profile than the intent specifies.

CHK-002:edge:1 (priority=should, type=cli) and CHK-002:edge:2 (priority=should, type=cli): both intents require the sub-field guards proven through the resolveAuditConfig integration path (via a tmpProject config file). CHK-002:edge:1 asks for non-integer maxConcurrentReview falling back via the integrated path; CHK-002:edge:2 asks for non-boolean broadGlobBlocks falling back via the integrated path. The smoke exercises both guards only through direct resolveParallelGate calls (lines 98-115), which satisfies the CHK-001 unit intents but not the CHK-002 cli/integration intents. No tmpProject({parallelGate:{maxConcurrentReview:2.5}}) or tmpProject({parallelGate:{broadGlobBlocks:'yes'}}) resolveAuditConfig call exists in the smoke.

CHK-001 userSees is empty — the checklist item defines what the implementer builds but does not describe the observable outcome (the user-visible contract): what does a caller of resolveParallelGate or resolveAuditConfig actually see? Missing userSees means behavioral correctness cannot be formally verified against a stated claim. Fill in userSees describing the resolved ParallelGateConfig values returned for each scenario (correct profile defaults, fallback to advise on bad mode, fallback to profile default on bad maxConcurrentReview/broadGlobBlocks, copy not reference on null input).
